description: Citywide non-emergency service requests; the demo pipeline filters to RODENT and SANITATION CONDITION complaints under the safety vertical.

core_columns.name: Created Date
core_columns.description: When the complaint was opened. Renamed to event_date in ready layer.

core_columns.name: Problem (formerly Complaint Type)
core_columns.description: Top-level complaint category. Renamed by NYC OD in 2024; downstream code must use the parenthetical.

core_columns.name: Incident Zip
core_columns.description: Five-digit ZIP. Note the space and 'Incident' prefix.

gotchas: Column was renamed by NYC OD: must reference 'Problem (formerly Complaint Type)' and 'Problem Detail (formerly Descriptor)' verbatim, including the parentheses.
ZIP column is 'Incident Zip' with a space, not 'Incident_Zip' or 'ZipCode'.
Demo preprocessing filters to a rodent/sanitation subset. The full dataset has hundreds of complaint types - do not assume safety_311_indexed.parquet contains everything.
Created Date strings include AM/PM; must parse with errors='coerce' to avoid NaT silently dropping rows.

sample_queries.intent: weekend rodent complaints in Brooklyn last 90 days
sample_queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('day', event_date) AS day, count(*) AS n FROM safety_311_indexed WHERE borough='BROOKLYN' AND extract(dow FROM event_date) IN (0,6) AND event_date >= now() - INTERVAL 90 DAY GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

sample_queries.intent: top h3 cells by sanitation complaint density
sample_queries.sql: SELECT h3_r9, raw_count, score FROM read_parquet('safety/311_scores_h3.parquet') ORDER BY raw_count DESC LIMIT 20

description: All police-reported NYC vehicle collisions since 2012. Drives both the safety risk score and a transit-vertical projection.

core_columns.name: CRASH DATE
core_columns.description: Date of crash. Renamed to event_date.

core_columns.name: NUMBER OF PEDESTRIANS INJURED
core_columns.description: Count column with spaces in the name.

gotchas: Column names contain spaces: 'CRASH DATE', 'ZIP CODE', 'NUMBER OF PEDESTRIANS INJURED' etc. SQL must double-quote them.
About 15% of rows have null lat/lon; pipeline drops them and clips to NYC bbox (40.45-40.95, -74.30 to -73.65).
Same indexed file is copied into both safety/ and transit/ output dirs (collision_transport_*) so the transit dimension has a score table.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT "ON STREET NAME", count(*) AS n FROM safety_collisions WHERE event_date >= '2024-01-01' AND "NUMBER OF PEDESTRIANS INJURED" > 0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10

description: DOH rodent inspections and bait records. Demo pipeline keeps only positive rat findings (RAT/FAILED/ACTIVE in RESULT).

core_columns.name: INSPECTION_DATE
core_columns.description: Date of inspection. Renamed to event_date.

core_columns.name: RESULT
core_columns.description: Inspection outcome string. Filter by RAT|FAILED|ACTIVE for positive findings.

core_columns.name: ZIP_CODE
core_columns.description: Note the underscore - different from collisions which uses a space.

gotchas: ZIP column is ZIP_CODE (underscore), unlike 311 (Incident Zip with space) and collisions (ZIP CODE with space). Three datasets, three conventions.
RESULT free-text varies; canonical positive set is regex RAT|FAILED|ACTIVE.
Rodent inspections cluster around complaint hotspots - interpret raw_count as 'attention received' not 'rats present'.

join_keys.note: Pair with 311 RODENT complaints to compare reported vs inspected.

sample_queries.intent: h3 cells with rising rodent inspections quarter over quarter
sample_queries.sql: SELECT h3_r9, quarter, count FROM read_parquet('safety/rodent_quarterly_h3.parquet') WHERE quarter >= '2024Q1' ORDER BY h3_r9, quarter

description: FDNY EMS dispatch records. Aggregated to ZIP-level average response time for the safety dimension.

core_columns.name: ZIPCODE
core_columns.description: Five-digit ZIP, no space. Renamed to zip.

core_columns.name: INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY
core_columns.description: Quality-validated response time in seconds. Use this column, not the raw INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS.

gotchas: MUST use the *_QY column (quality-validated): INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS_QY, not INCIDENT_RESPONSE_SECONDS. Raw is unvalidated.
Some upstream guides recommend filtering valid='Y'; current preprocess relies on the _QY suffix instead.
Aggregated by ZIP, not by lat/lon (no point geometry in source). Joins to other datasets must go through ZIP.
Average response time has very low variance; old linear scoring collapsed to 60+/-5 - pipeline now uses percentile ranking.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT zip, avg_response_seconds, score FROM read_parquet('safety/ems_scores_zip.parquet') ORDER BY avg_response_seconds DESC LIMIT 20

description: FDNY fire dispatch records. Same shape as EMS but uses INCIDENT_BOROUGH instead of BOROUGH.

core_columns.name: INCIDENT_BOROUGH
core_columns.description: Borough - column is INCIDENT_BOROUGH here, just BOROUGH in the EMS table.

gotchas: Borough column is INCIDENT_BOROUGH (Fire) but BOROUGH (EMS). Do not blindly UNION ALL the two without aliasing.
Same _QY rule as EMS: use the validated time column.
Both EMS and Fire are aggregated to ZIP-level; lat/lon are not in the ready layer.

sample_queries.intent: compare EMS vs Fire response time by borough
sample_queries.sql: SELECT e.borough, avg(e.avg_response_seconds) AS ems_avg, avg(f.avg_response_seconds) AS fire_avg FROM safety_ems e JOIN safety_fire f USING(zip) GROUP BY 1

description: MTA subway entrance and exit point geometry, used as the proxy for subway access score.
primary_key: Stop Name + Entrance Latitude + Entrance Longitude

core_columns.name: Entrance Latitude
core_columns.description: Per-entrance latitude. Note: NOT a generic 'Latitude' column - pipeline renames to latitude.

gotchas: Each station has multiple entrance rows. Counting raw rows overstates 'station density'; deduplicate by Stop Name if you need station counts.
Use Entrance Latitude/Longitude - there is no plain Latitude column.
access_mode=True scoring: more entrances per H3 cell = higher score (good).

sample_queries.intent: h3 cells with subway entrances but low bus shelter coverage
sample_queries.sql: SELECT s.h3_r9, s.raw_count AS subway, coalesce(b.raw_count, 0) AS bus FROM read_parquet('transit/subway_scores_h3.parquet') s LEFT JOIN read_parquet('transit/bus_scores_h3.parquet') b USING(h3_r9) WHERE s.raw_count >= 3 AND coalesce(b.raw_count, 0) = 0

description: Locations of MTA bus stop shelters maintained by JCDecaux.

core_columns.name: Cross_Stre
core_columns.description: Cross street - note the truncated name 'Cross_Stre' in the source CSV.

core_columns.name: BoroName
core_columns.description: Borough - column name is BoroName, not Borough.

gotchas: Cross street column is truncated to 'Cross_Stre' in the source CSV.
Borough column is BoroName (camel case + truncation) not BOROUGH or Borough.
Only shelters, not all bus stops - true bus stop coverage is much higher than shelter coverage.

sample_queries.intent: neighborhoods with bus shelters but no subway
sample_queries.sql: SELECT b.h3_r9 FROM read_parquet('transit/bus_scores_h3.parquet') b LEFT JOIN read_parquet('transit/subway_scores_h3.parquet') s USING(h3_r9) WHERE s.raw_count IS NULL AND b.raw_count >= 2

description: DOT bike lane geometry as WKT MULTILINESTRING. Pipeline extracts vertices and counts distinct segments per H3 cell.

core_columns.name: the_geom
core_columns.description: WKT MULTILINESTRING geometry. Lowercase column name.

gotchas: Geometry is WKT, not lat/lon points. Pipeline uses regex to extract coordinate pairs - no shapely dependency.
WKT order is 'lon lat' (per OGC), not 'lat lon'. Easy to swap.
Per-cell count uses distinct (h3_r9, record_index) pairs to avoid thick polylines inflating density.
Column name is lowercase 'the_geom'; the open_streets sibling uses 'The_Geom' with capitals.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT boro, count(DISTINCT segmentid) FROM transit_bike_routes_indexed GROUP BY 1

description: Streets temporarily closed to vehicle traffic for pedestrian use.

core_columns.name: Object ID
core_columns.description: Two-word column name with a space.

core_columns.name: The_Geom
core_columns.description: WKT geometry. Note the capitalization 'The_Geom' (different from bike routes).

gotchas: WKT column is 'The_Geom' (mixed case), bike routes uses lowercase 'the_geom'.
Many column names contain spaces ('Object ID', 'Borough Name', 'Approved On Street') - quote them in SQL.
Same vertex extraction as bike routes.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT "Borough Name", count(*) FROM transit_open_streets GROUP BY 1

dataset_name: DOHMH New York City Restaurant Inspection Results
description: Restaurant health inspections. Pipeline scores both abundance (more = more access) and quality (lower critical-flag rate = better).

core_columns.name: CAMIS
core_columns.description: Restaurant id (City Agency Management Information System).

core_columns.name: CRITICAL FLAG
core_columns.description: Critical / Not Critical / Not Applicable. Used for quality score.

core_columns.name: ZIPCODE
core_columns.description: All caps ZIPCODE - different from collisions ('ZIP CODE') and 311 ('Incident Zip').

gotchas: CRITICAL FLAG values include 'Critical', 'Not Critical', 'Not Applicable'. Match case-insensitively after upper().
BORO is truncated; do not look for BOROUGH.
The same restaurant (CAMIS) appears in many rows (one per inspection). To count distinct restaurants, use COUNT(DISTINCT CAMIS).
Score is a 50/50 blend of percentile-rank abundance and inverse-percentile-rank critical_rate.

sample_queries.intent: best-scored amenity h3 cells (high access AND low critical rate)
sample_queries.sql: SELECT h3_r9, raw_count, critical_rate, score FROM read_parquet('amenities/restaurants_scores_h3.parquet') ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 20

description: NYC Parks portfolio. Aggregated to ZIP-level total acreage; score is percentile rank of total park acres per ZIP.

core_columns.name: ACRES
core_columns.description: Total acreage. Renamed to 'value' in pipeline.

gotchas: v3.7.8 fix: score is computed from total ACRES per ZIP, not from record count. Counting park polygons under-weights large parks.
Some parks span multiple ZIPs but the source row only lists one - under-counts edge ZIPs.
WATERFRONT is a free text Y/N; do not assume boolean.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT zip, total_value AS total_acres, score FROM read_parquet('amenities/parks_scores_zip.parquet') ORDER BY total_value DESC LIMIT 20

description: Per-tree census from 2015 (frozen snapshot, no longer updated).

core_columns.name: created_at
core_columns.description: Census record date. Renamed to event_date.

core_columns.name: postcode
core_columns.description: ZIP - column name is 'postcode' (lowercase, no underscore). Renamed to zip.

gotchas: Snapshot dataset from 2015 - no longer updated. Use as a baseline, not a real-time signal.
All column names are lowercase, unlike most other NYC OD tables.
Status='Dead' or 'Stump' rows are still counted in raw_count; filter to status='Alive' for usable canopy.

sample_queries.intent: tree canopy score by h3 cell
sample_queries.sql: SELECT h3_r9, raw_count, score FROM read_parquet('amenities/trees_scores_h3.parquet') ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 20

description: LinkNYC public Wi-Fi / phone kiosk locations.

core_columns.name: Site ID
core_columns.description: Two-word column name with a space.

core_columns.name: Postcode
core_columns.description: ZIP - column 'Postcode', not Postal Code or ZIPCODE.

gotchas: Multiple column-name conventions ('Site ID', 'Street Address') - quote them in SQL.
Installation Status='Live' is the only status that should count toward 'access'; pipeline does not filter by default.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT borough, count(*) FROM amenities_linknyc WHERE "Installation Status" = 'Live' GROUP BY 1

dataset_name: Directory Of Toilets In Public Parks
gotchas: No ZIP, no borough column - pipeline derives them from H3 lookup if needed.
Status free-text varies; treat as access proxy without filtering by default.
Very small dataset - most H3 cells have 0; score gradient is sparse.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT h3_r9, raw_count FROM read_parquet('amenities/toilets_scores_h3.parquet') WHERE raw_count > 0

description: Cross-agency master directory of city-owned, leased, or regulated facilities (schools, libraries, clinics, transportation hubs, etc).
gotchas: All lowercase columns. Renamed by pipeline (zipcode->zip, boro->borough).
facgroup and facsubgrp form a 2-level hierarchy with ~20 groups and ~150 sub-groups; use them to filter to a specific facility class instead of joining other tables.
Facilities Database can substitute for transit if MTA datasets are unusable: filter facgroup='Transportation' for transit hubs.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT zip, count(*) FROM amenities_facilities_indexed WHERE facsubgrp ILIKE '%K-12%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

description: HPD housing code violations. Pipeline filters to open violations (ViolationStatus not containing 'CLOSE').

core_columns.name: InspectionDate
core_columns.description: When violation was issued. Renamed to event_date.

core_columns.name: ViolationStatus
core_columns.description: Open/Close - pipeline filters on this column, not CurrentStatus.

core_columns.name: BBL
core_columns.description: Borough-Block-Lot - primary parcel join key. 10 digits.

gotchas: Pipeline filters where ViolationStatus does NOT contain 'CLOSE'. The CurrentStatus column has more granular state but is not used as the open/closed filter.
BBL is the canonical parcel join key. Always 10 digits; pad with leading zeros if upstream lost them.
Class C violations are most severe (immediately hazardous) - surface them in any 'building safety' query.
PLUTO does not carry BIN - to bridge violations to a specific building structure you need an HPD bridge table (out of scope for v2; rely on BBL).

sample_queries.intent: open Class C violations by borough
sample_queries.sql: SELECT borough, count(*) FROM building_violations_indexed WHERE Class='C' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

description: Alternative Enforcement Program (HPD's distressed building program). Pipeline filters to active (not discharged) buildings.

core_columns.name: CURRENT_STATUS
core_columns.description: AEP status string. Filter excludes rows containing 'DISCHARG' (active = not discharged).

core_columns.name: AEP_START_DATE
core_columns.description: Date entered AEP. Renamed to event_date.

gotchas: Tiny dataset (~4K buildings) but high-signal - these are the city's most distressed properties.
Mixed case conventions: BUILDING_ID + CURRENT_STATUS are caps_with_underscore; Postcode + Latitude are camel case.
Same BBL bridge as building_violations - joining the two tables is the canonical 'is this building both AEP and currently in violation?' query.

sample_queries.intent: active AEP buildings with class C violations
sample_queries.sql: SELECT a.BBL, count(*) FROM building_aep_indexed a JOIN building_violations_indexed v ON a.BBL = v.BBL WHERE v.Class='C' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20

dataset_name: Primary Land Use Tax Lot Output (PLUTO)
description: Tax lot reference table. Acts as the canonical address / BBL / lat-lon resolver for every other building dataset.

core_columns.name: appbbl
core_columns.description: Apportionment BBL - for lots that have been merged/split, this is the previous BBL.

gotchas: PLUTO does NOT contain BIN. To map a lot to a specific building you need a separate bridge (HPD Buildings or DOB Buildings).
Use BBL as the join key for everything building-related. Use appbbl as a fallback when BBL is null.
canonical_location_id is computed as 'pluto_<BBL>' for downstream agent reference.
PLUTO refreshes ~3 times a year; lot geometry can change between vintages.

sample_queries.sql: SELECT BBL, address, borough, zip FROM location_pluto WHERE BBL = ?
